data.name: Nalakshi
data.gender_notes: Nalakshi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the words 'nala' (star) and 'akshi' (eye), Nalakshi signifies a person who maps or navigates by stars. The name Nalakshi carries the meaning “Star Mapper” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nalakshi usually hope their child will grow to embody star mapper and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Nalakshi belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Star Mapper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nalakshi total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Nalakshi is an evocative name rooted in ancient Indian astronomical knowledge and navigational prowess. The name reflects the Hindu tradition of revering celestial bodies for guidance and understanding the cosmos. It is a reminder of India's rich history and contribution to the science and art of astronomy.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Hindu spiritual tradition, eyes are considered the windows to the soul, symbolizing inner-vision and awareness. Nalakshi represents the spiritual guide who navigates not just through the physical world, but also through the intricacies of life and the complexities of the human spirit. It is aname that inspires the inner ability to see beyond the ordinary and to traverse the spiritual path with clarity and purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nalakshi: The radiant, blue-throated form of Shiva, symbolizing the destructive and creative aspects of life, embodied in the deity's name. This name evokes a balance between destruction and creation, symbolizing the cyclic nature of existence.

vedic_reference.note: Not from Vedas, Upanishads, or other scriptures.

historical_references.reference: Nalakshi is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the name of a divine form of God Vishnu. Nalakshi is depicted as having four arms, each holding a weapon and a lotus flower, and a serpent coiled around his neck.

Another reference to Nalakshi comes from the Puranic literature, which describes Nalakshi as the presiding deity of the town of Thiruvidandhai, near Kumbakonam in Tamil Nadu, India. Nalakshi is believed to have appeared before a local king in the form of a beautiful woman to grant him a boon.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nalakshi is derived from Hindu mythology, where it is the name of a goddess associated with wealth, prosperity, and good fortune. In modern contexts, this name is often seen in various artistic expressions and fashion trends. On Instagram, one can find multiple posts featuring artworks, illustrations, and paintings inspired by the goddess Nalakshi. On Pinterest, there are numerous pins displaying home decor, clothing, and jewelry items inspired by this deity. Etsy, an online marketplace, is filled with various Nalakshi-themed products, including jewelry, wall art, and clothing.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Lakshmi Nalakshi in Bangalore, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Nalakshi, which means "Star Mapper". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
